units.title: Basic Economics Concepts
units.intro: **Scarcity:** wants exceed what resources can make. That forces **choice**. The next-best thing you drop is **opportunity cost**. Economics studies how people, firms and governments choose under scarcity to satisfy material wants as well as they can.

f1.title: On the curve = efficient. Inside = wasted resources. Outside = impossible today. Growth pushes the curve out.

cards.title: 1.0 Introduction to Economics
body: The choices that individuals and societies make in response to scarcity are the subject matter of economics.
**Economics** is the science of making choices with the objective to meet human wants as much as possible.
**Economics** is the study of how individuals and societies choose to use their scarce resources in order to satisfy their material wants as much as possible.
**Economics** is a social science concerned with the efficient use of limited (scarce) resources to achieve maximum satisfaction of human material wants.
Scarcity will always exist and cannot be eliminated in all societies; it is a universal economic problem.

cards.title: Formula
body: Opportunity cost = value of the next-best alternative
Not “everything you could have done” — only the best rejected option.

cards.title: Introduction to Economics
body: **Three questions:** what to produce, how, for whom. **Factors:** land, labour, capital, entrepreneurship. Systems: traditional, command, market, mixed. Most countries are mixed — markets plus a government that taxes, spends and sets rules.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: Which of the following is the primary reason why economic choices must be made in all societies?

steps.text: **Step 1: Understand the economic problem**
Scarcity is defined as the situation where resources are insufficient to satisfy all human wants.
**Step 2: Relate to Choice**
Because resources are limited ($$\text{Resources} < \text{Wants}$$), individuals and societies cannot have everything they desire.
Therefore, they are forced to make choices.

cards.answer: The coexistence of limited resources and unlimited wants

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: A production possibilities curve that is concave (bowed outward) from the origin indicates which of the following?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Understand the shape of the PPC**
A concave (bowed-outward) PPC indicates that as you produce more of one good, the amount of the other good you must sacrifice increases.

**Step 2: Relate to the Law of Increasing Opportunity Cost**
This occurs because economic resources are specialized and not equally adaptable to the production of both goods.

**Step 3: Conclusion**
Therefore, a concave curve represents **increasing opportunity costs**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: In which economic system are all resources owned and allocated by the government?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Define resource ownership in command economies**
In a command economic system (centrally planned economy), all productive resources (land, capital, factories) are owned by the public, managed by the state/government.

**Step 2: Identify the allocation mechanism**
Decisions on what, how, and for whom to produce are dictated by a central planning authority.

**Step 3: Match options**
This aligns with the **Command economic system**.

cards.title: Identifying the factors of production
cards.problem: A farmer near Keren grows vegetables on her land, hires two workers, uses a water pump and decides what to plant and where to sell. Identify the factors of production and the reward each one earns.

steps.text: Land – the farm plot and its water (natural resources); reward = rent.
Labour – the two hired workers (and the farmer's own physical work); reward = wages.
Capital – the water pump and tools (man-made aids to production); reward = interest.
Entrepreneurship – the farmer who organizes, decides and takes the risk; reward = profit.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The four factors of production are ____.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Production combines resources called factors of production.

**Step 2:** They are land (natural resources), labour (human effort), capital (man-made tools) and entrepreneurship (organising and taking risk).

**Step 3:** Their rewards are rent, wages, interest and profit.

**Tip:** Read every option against the rule before choosing.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Turning cotton into cloth in a textile factory is an example of:
cards.why:

**Step 2:** Cotton (input) is processed into cloth (output).

**Step 3:** Answer: production.

**Tip:** Production also includes services – a teacher or a transporter is a producer too.

cards.title: 1.2 Business Organizations
body: In their daily life individuals consume various goods and services.
Business organisations sell their goods and services to buyers in the marketplace to earn profits, while buyers purchase them to satisfy their wants.
Business organization refers to any private organization which employs factors of production to produce goods and services for profit.
A business organization may be commercial such as grocery; professional such as providing legal service giving; or an industrial organization such as a shoe making firm.
Sole Proprietorship (sole trader) Sole Proprietorship is the simplest form of business.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which branch of economics deals with aggregates such as inflation, gross national income, and the overall unemployment rate of a country?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Differentiate Microeconomics vs. Macroeconomics**
- Microeconomics: Focuses on individual decision-making units (e.g., a single consumer or firm).
- Macroeconomics: Focuses on the aggregate economy as a whole (e.g., total output, inflation, general price level, national unemployment).

**Step 2: Select the correct term**
Aggregates like national income and inflation fall under **Macroeconomics**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: A business organization in which all decisions are made by a single owner is
cards.why: A **sole proprietorship** is a business owned and operated by one person. The owner has total control over all decisions and receives all profits, but also carries unlimited liability.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: An entrepreneur starting a sole proprietorship faces which of the following legal financial characteristics?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Define Sole Proprietorship characteristics**
A sole proprietorship is owned by a single individual. legally, there is no separation between the business entity and the personal owner.

**Step 2: Understand the liability consequences**
Because there is no legal separation, the owner faces **unlimited liability**, meaning personal assets can be seized to pay off business debts.

**Step 3: Conclusion**
Therefore, the correct answer is **Unlimited liability**.

Because there is no legal separation, the owner faces **unlimited liability**, meaning personal assets can be seized to pay off business debts.
**Step 3: Conclusion**
Therefore, the correct answer is **Unlimited liability**.

cards.title: 1.3 Transportation and Communication
body: In the present world no business can survive without modern communication and transportation systems.

People in the different parts of the world are connected by a network of modern transportation and communication systems, which facilitate the movement of goods and people as well as the transfer of information.
Transportation and communication facilitate trade within a country and among the different countries of the world.
In modem societies, it is very rare to find goods being produced in places where they are wanted or fully consumed.
Often, goods are produced in some places, and they are consumed in other places.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What is the primary function of communication in business?

options.B: To coordinate the factors of production and facilitate information flow
options.C: To maximize the rate of double taxation
options.D: To reduce the number of shareholders

cards.why:
**Step 1: Understand business coordination requirements**
A business must coordinate land, labor, and capital to produce efficiently. This requires constant, accurate sharing of instructions and market data.

**Step 2: Identify the role of communication**
Communication facilitates this coordination by enabling the flow of information between management, suppliers, and customers.

**Step 3: Match options**
This aligns with 'To coordinate the factors of production and facilitate information flow'.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The historical Massawa-Asmara ropeway, constructed during the Italian colonial period, was dismantled by which authority?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Recall the historical timeline of the Eritrean ropeway**
The $$71\text{ km}$$ ropeway was constructed during the Italian colonial period to connect the Port of Massawa with Asmara.

**Step 2: Identify when and by whom it was dismantled**
Following the defeat of Italy in World War II, the British took administration of Eritrea and dismantled the ropeway, selling it for scrap.

**Step 3: Select the correct option**
This corresponds to the **British Administration**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following types of transportation systems is appropriate to transport heavy and bulky goods for long distances?
cards.why: Water transport (shipping) is the most economical way to move very heavy, bulky, and large quantities of goods across long international distances, though it is slower than other methods.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which mode of transport is the most appropriate and cost-effective for moving extremely bulky, heavy, non-perishable goods across international borders?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Evaluate transportation mode constraints**
- Air: Fast, but very expensive and limited weight capacity.
- Road: Flexible, but restricted by land borders and low capacity per vehicle.
- Water: Slow, but lowest cost per unit and designed for huge bulk over long oceanic distances.

**Step 2: Conclusion**
For international, heavy, bulky, non-perishable cargo, **Water transportation** is the most cost-effective.

glossary.meaning: Scarcity of resources is the inability of societies to produce enough goods and/or services to satisfy all their material wants and needs.
Economics is the science of making choices with the objective to meet human wants as much as possible.
Production is the transformation of inputs into outputs by business firms.
Human capital is the economic characterization of the education and training of workers.
Labour is the most active factor of production.
Opportunity cost is the amount of goods that must be sacrificed to obtain a unit of another good.
Wealth is the sum of all the assets accumulated over time by a society or a country.
Welfare is the state of well-being of a society.
Microeconomics is a branch of economics that studies the economic behavior of individual decisionmaking units such as consumers and business firms.
Corporation is a egal entity, distinct and separate from the individuals who own it.
Transportation is the safe movement of goods (freight) and people from one place to another.
Water transportation is the safe movement of goods and people through the routes of water bodies such ocean, sea, river, lake or canal.
Air transportation is the safe movement of goods and people from one place to another using air routes.
Communication is the transfer (or exchange) of any kind of information from one person or place to another person or place.
Communication system is a combination of processes and hardware (instruments) used to accomplish the transfer of information (communication).

tips.text: The basic problem of any society is how to use its available resources to meet its wants.
Scarcity of resources is the basic fact of life.
Available resources (factors of production) are scarce in relation to our desires for goods and services.
Resources everywhere are in limited supply (scarce). These questions are answered in different ways under different economic systems.
Economic system refers to the way a society allocates its resources and makes the three economic decisions.
The three economic systems differ in the method of allocating the resources and ownership of the resources.
Production is the process by which factors of production (scarce resources) are changed into goods and services demanded by a society.
The major factors of production are land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship.
Land is considered as fixed in quantity.
Society uses resources or factors of production to produce various goods and services to satisfy human wants.
Formula: Opportunity cost = value of the next-best alternative Not “everything you could have done” — only the best rejected option.

questions.answer: Resources are scarce relative to wants.
why: Human wants are unlimited but the resources to satisfy them (land, labour, capital, time) are limited, so people, firms and governments must choose which wants to satisfy.
questions.label: 1. Why is choice necessary?
questions.tip: Say or write your answer first, then open the model answer and compare the key words.

similar.q: Economics is the study of how  A) scarce resources are used to satisfy unlimited wants  B) we choose to use unlimited resources  C) limitless resources are used to satisfy scarce wants  D) society has no choices  E) All of the above
similar.a: A. scarce resources are used to satisfy unlimited wants — B and C reverse the relationship (resources are not unlimited, wants are not scarce); D is wrong because scarcity forces choices. Answer: A.

questions.answer: The best other use of that evening (work, rest) — pick one, not a list.
why: Opportunity cost is only the single best alternative given up — e.g. the money you could have earned working that evening — not the sum of all alternatives.
questions.label: 2. Opportunity cost of studying tonight?
questions.tip: Say or write your answer first, then open the model answer and compare the key words.

similar.q: The highest alternative forgone to get your best choice defines the concept of  A) opportunity cost.  B) scarcity.  C) entrepreneurship.  D) economics.  E) politics.
similar.a: A. opportunity cost. — Answer: A.

questions.answer: Unemployed or wasted resources — you can have more of both goods.
why: A point inside the production possibility curve means the economy is producing less than it could: some resources are unemployed or used inefficiently.
questions.label: 3. Point inside the PPC means?
questions.tip: Say or write your answer first, then open the model answer and compare the key words.

similar.q: The production possibility curve (PPC) shows  A) the maximum amount of resources that an economy possesses.  B) the maximum amount of two goods that an economy can produce with fixed resources.  C) the unlimited resources of an economy.  D) all of the goods an economy can produce while leaving some resources idle.  E) the maximum amount of goods an economy can consume.
similar.a: B. the maximum amount of two goods that an economy can produce with fixed resources. — Idle resources give points INSIDE the curve (D). Answer: B.

questions.answer: Impossible with current resources and technology.
why: Points outside the PPC cannot be produced with the existing resources and technology; they become possible only if the curve shifts outward.
questions.label: 4. Point outside?
questions.tip: Say or write your answer first, then open the model answer and compare the key words.

similar.q: A point lies outside the production possibility curve represents:  A) inefficient  B) efficient  C) unattainable  D) attainable  E) None of the above
similar.a: C. unattainable — Points OUTSIDE (beyond) the PPC cannot be produced with the currently available resources and technology → unattainable. Answer: C.

questions.answer: More resources, better tech, better skills.
why: The PPC shifts outward when the economy can produce more of both goods: more or better resources (labour, capital), improved technology or better education and skills.
questions.label: 5. What shifts the PPC out?
questions.tip: Say or write your answer first, then open the model answer and compare the key words.

similar.q: Four factors of production?
similar.a: Land, labour, capital, enterprise.

questions.answer: Land, labour, capital, enterprise.
why: The factors of production are land (natural resources), labour (human effort), capital (man-made tools and machines) and enterprise (organising and risk-taking).
questions.label: 6. Four factors of production?
questions.tip: Say or write your answer first, then open the model answer and compare the key words.

similar.a: C. command, market and mixed. — Of the options only C lists economic systems (B = economic agents, E = factors of production). Answer: C.

questions.answer: Produced means of production (tools, machines) — not only money.
why: In economics capital means man-made goods used to produce other goods — machines, tools, buildings, vehicles — not money itself.
questions.label: 7. Capital in economics is?
questions.tip: Say or write your answer first, then open the model answer and compare the key words.

similar.q: What / how / for whom?
similar.a: The three allocation questions.

questions.answer: The three allocation questions.
why: Every economy must decide what to produce, how to produce it (which methods and resources) and for whom (how output is distributed).
questions.label: 8. What / how / for whom?
questions.tip: Say or write your answer first, then open the model answer and compare the key words.

similar.q: Problems relating to the allocation of factors of production and the distribution of income exist in  A) command economies only.  B) capitalist economies only.  C) traditional economies only.  D) mixed economies only.  E) all economies.
similar.a: E. all economies. — Economic systems differ only in HOW they answer these questions (custom, government planning, the market, or a mix). Answer: E.

questions.answer: Prices and voluntary trade.
why: In a market economy, prices set by supply and demand signal what consumers want; producers seeking profit respond, and goods go to those willing and able to pay.
questions.label: 9. Market system answers them by?
questions.tip: Say or write your answer first, then open the model answer and compare the key words.

similar.q: An increase in the price of beef provides  A) information that tells consumers to buy more beef.  B) information that tells consumers to buy less pork.  C) information that tells producers to produce more beef.  D) no information because prices in a market system are managed by planning boards.  E) None of the above.
similar.a: C. information that tells producers to produce more beef. — Consumers would switch TO pork (a substitute), not buy less of it; prices are not set by planning boards in a market system. Answer: C.

questions.answer: A central plan.
why: In a command (planned) economy the government owns most resources and a central plan decides what, how and for whom to produce.
questions.label: 10. Command system answers them by?
questions.tip: Say or write your answer first, then open the model answer and compare the key words.

similar.q: An economic system  A) requires a grouping of private markets linked to one another.  B) refers to the way a society allocates its scarce resources and makes the three economic decisions.  C) requires a centralized authority to coordinate economic activity.  D) is a plan which allows a firm to make profit at some other firm’s expense.  E) None of the above.
similar.a: B. refers to the way a society allocates its scarce resources and makes the three economic decisions. — A describes only a market economy and C only a command economy. Answer: B.

questions.answer: Markets plus government.
why: A mixed economy combines private markets with government involvement — the state provides public services and regulates, while private firms produce most goods.

questions.answer: Is vs ought.
why: Positive statements describe what is and can be tested with facts ("prices rose 5%"); normative statements say what ought to be and involve value judgements ("prices should be controlled").

why: Microeconomics studies individual units — households, firms, single markets; macroeconomics studies the whole economy — national income, inflation, unemployment.

similar.a: D. a capital good. — The machine is not used up in one cup and is not consumed. Answer: D.

similar.q: The opportunity cost of your attending college is the  A) cost of tuition, books and fees.  B) cost of room and board in the dorms if you live in campus.  C) wages you could have earned in a job if you were not attending college.  D) All of the above.  E) None of the above.
similar.a: C. wages you could have earned in a job if you were not attending college. — In a full economic analysis tuition, books and fees are also part of the cost of going to college, but they are money (explicit) costs; the classic answer to this test item is the forgone wages. Answer: C.

why: Resources have alternative uses but are limited; using them for one good means less of another — the idea of scarcity and trade-off shown by the PPC.

similar.q: Economics is the study of how  A) to fully satisfy our unlimited wants.  B) society manages its scarce resources.  C) to reduce our wants until we are satisfied.  D) to avoid having to make trade-offs.  E) society manages its limited wants and unlimited resources.
similar.a: B. society manages its scarce resources. — Wants can never be fully satisfied (A), scarcity forces trade-offs (D), and E reverses ‘limited’ and ‘unlimited’. Answer: B.

questions.answer: B
why: Answer B: The next-best alternative given up
Opportunity cost is only the next-best alternative forgone, not every alternative added together.
